phases.name: Foundations
phases.description: Tools and habits you will reuse in every later project.

phases.name: Building blocks
phases.description: Small components that later systems are made of. Keep them; you will import them later.

phases.name: Classic product systems
phases.description: End-to-end services with an API, storage, cache and queue.

phases.name: Geo and real-time location
phases.description: Spatial indexes, routing and streaming location updates.

phases.name: Data infrastructure
phases.description: The systems other systems run on: logs, metrics, streams and blobs.

phases.name: Money and correctness
phases.description: Concurrency, idempotency, ledgers and determinism, where bugs cost real money.

phases.name: Fundamentals deep dives
phases.description: Theory, networking, APIs, databases, replication and caching: the vocabulary under every design.

phases.name: Distributed patterns
phases.description: Async work, transactions, concurrency, memory, resilience and scaling economics.

phases.name: Production engineering
phases.description: Containers, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, releases, observability, schema changes, DR and incidents.

phases.name: Security
phases.description: Identity, secrets, encryption and web application attacks and defences.

chapters.title: Scale from Zero to Millions of Users
chapters.goal: Take one tiny web app from a single box to a load-balanced, replicated, cached deployment on your laptop, and measure what each step buys you.
chapters.short: Nginx + replicas + Postgres replica + Redis cache, load tested

chapters.title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
chapters.goal: Build a small estimation toolkit you will reuse in every later chapter, and calibrate your intuition by measuring real latencies on your own machine.
chapters.short: Estimation toolkit + latency bench

chapters.title: A Framework for System Design Interviews
chapters.goal: Turn the 4-step framework into a habit: a design-doc template you fill for every chapter, plus a timer that runs you through a 45-minute mock.
chapters.short: Design template + 45-min mock timer

chapters.title: Design a Rate Limiter
chapters.goal: Implement all five rate-limiting algorithms, then ship one of them as distributed middleware backed by Redis.
chapters.short: 5 algorithms + Redis Lua limiter middleware

chapters.title: Design Consistent Hashing
chapters.goal: Build a consistent hash ring with virtual nodes and prove, with numbers, that it moves far fewer keys than `hash % N`.
chapters.short: Hash ring with vnodes + key-movement experiment

chapters.title: Design a Key-Value Store
chapters.goal: Build a mini Dynamo/Cassandra: an LSM storage engine on one node, then a 3+ node cluster with quorum reads/writes, vector clocks and hinted handoff.
chapters.short: LSM engine + quorum cluster with vector clocks

chapters.title: Design a Unique ID Generator
chapters.goal: Build a Snowflake-style 64-bit ID service and stress it for uniqueness, ordering and clock skew, then compare against UUIDs and a ticket server.
chapters.short: Snowflake ID service

chapters.title: Design a URL Shortener
chapters.goal: Ship a working TinyURL clone: base62 short codes from your chapter 7 IDs, cached redirects, and click analytics.
chapters.short: TinyURL clone with cache + analytics

chapters.title: Design a Web Crawler
chapters.goal: Build a polite, distributed-ready crawler with a real URL frontier (priority + politeness queues), run against a local fake web so you can crawl millions of pages safely.
chapters.short: Polite crawler over a fake local web

chapters.title: Design a Notification System
chapters.goal: Build a multi-channel notification service (push, SMS, email) with per-channel queues, retries, dedupe, user settings and delivery tracking, using mock providers that fail on purpose.
chapters.short: Multi-channel notifier with retries + dedupe

chapters.title: Design a News Feed System
chapters.goal: Build a feed service with fan-out on write for normal users and fan-out on read for celebrities, and measure the trade-off.
chapters.short: Hybrid fan-out feed on Redis

chapters.title: Design a Chat System
chapters.goal: Build a WebSocket chat with 1:1 and small group chats, per-channel message ordering, multi-device sync and online presence via heartbeats.
chapters.short: WebSocket chat with sync + presence

chapters.title: Design a Search Autocomplete System
chapters.goal: Build a typeahead service: a trie with cached top-k at every node, rebuilt offline from a query log, served fast from memory.
chapters.short: Top-k trie typeahead service

chapters.title: Design YouTube
chapters.goal: Build a mini video platform: resumable upload to object storage, a DAG-based transcoding pipeline with ffmpeg producing HLS renditions, and adaptive streaming playback.
chapters.short: Upload + ffmpeg DAG transcoding + HLS playback

chapters.title: Design Google Drive
chapters.goal: Build a Dropbox-like sync client and server: block-level chunking with dedupe, delta upload, file versioning, conflict detection and change notifications via long polling.
chapters.short: Block-level sync client + server

chapters.title: Proximity Service
chapters.goal: Build a Yelp-style "businesses near me" service and implement geohash and quadtree indexes yourself, then compare them with PostGIS.
chapters.short: Geohash + quadtree "near me" search

chapters.title: Nearby Friends
chapters.goal: Build a real-time "friends near you" feature: clients stream locations over WebSockets, servers fan them out to friends through Redis pub/sub, and only nearby updates reach the user.
chapters.short: Live nearby friends over WebSockets + pub/sub

chapters.title: Google Maps
chapters.goal: Build the three pillars of a maps product at city scale: a tile server, a routing service on a real road graph with A*, and a location ingestion pipeline that feeds live traffic into ETAs.
chapters.short: Tile server + A* routing on OSM + live ETA

chapters.title: Distributed Message Queue
chapters.goal: Build a mini Kafka: segmented append-only logs per partition, offsets, consumer groups with committed offsets, batching, and leader/follower replication with ISR.
chapters.short: Mini Kafka: segmented log, groups, replication

chapters.title: Metrics Monitoring and Alerting System
chapters.goal: Build a small Prometheus/Datadog: agents push metrics through a queue into your own time-series store, with a query API, downsampling, alert rules and a Grafana dashboard.
chapters.short: Mini Prometheus: TSDB, rollups, alerting

chapters.title: Ad Click Event Aggregation
chapters.goal: Build a streaming pipeline that counts ad clicks per minute and the top-N ads, with event-time windows, watermarks for late events, dedupe and exactly-once offsets, then reconcile against a batch job.
chapters.short: Windowed click aggregation with watermarks

chapters.title: Hotel Reservation System
chapters.goal: Build a booking service that never double-books, even under heavy concurrency, and compare pessimistic locking, optimistic locking and DB constraints with real measurements.
chapters.short: No-double-booking reservation API

chapters.title: Distributed Email Service
chapters.goal: Build a small Gmail: receive mail over SMTP, store metadata and bodies separately, serve folders and threads over a web API with real-time updates, and add full-text search.
chapters.short: SMTP-in mail service with threads + search

chapters.title: S3-like Object Storage
chapters.goal: Build a mini S3: a metadata service, data nodes that pack small objects into large append-only files, checksums, versioning, multipart upload and garbage collection.
chapters.short: Mini S3: packed data files, versioning, GC

chapters.title: Real-time Gaming Leaderboard
chapters.goal: Build a real-time monthly leaderboard on Redis sorted sets, then implement the skip list underneath yourself to understand why it's O(log n).
chapters.short: Skip-list + Redis sorted-set leaderboard

chapters.title: Payment System
chapters.goal: Build a pay-in flow end to end: checkout -> payment service -> mock PSP with a hosted payment page and webhooks -> double-entry ledger -> wallet, plus retries, idempotency and nightly reconciliation.
chapters.short: Pay-in flow with mock PSP + double-entry ledger

chapters.title: Digital Wallet
chapters.goal: Build a wallet that moves money between accounts with an auditable event log: event sourcing with replayable state, snapshots, and a distributed transfer across shards using TC/C and Saga.
chapters.short: Event-sourced wallet with TC/C + Saga

chapters.title: Stock Exchange
chapters.goal: Build a low-latency exchange core: order manager with risk checks, a sequencer, a price-time-priority matching engine, market data (L1/L2 and candlesticks), and deterministic replay from the event log.
chapters.short: Matching engine + sequencer + market data

chapters.title: Principles & Theorems
chapters.goal: Get the theory every design argument leans on into your hands: CAP and PACELC, eventual consistency, latency vs throughput, percentiles and tail latency, network partitions and clock skew.
chapters.short: Percentiles, tail latency, quorums, Lamport clocks

chapters.title: Networking & Protocols
chapters.goal: Understand what's under every RPC: DNS resolution and caching, TCP vs UDP, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3, and gRPC's wire format.
chapters.short: Varints, gRPC frames, DNS resolver + cache

chapters.title: APIs & the Edge
chapters.goal: Build the layer between clients and services: a reverse proxy with weighted load balancing, an API gateway that routes by version, and signed webhooks.
chapters.short: Weighted LB, versioned gateway, signed webhooks

chapters.title: Real-time Transports
chapters.goal: Compare the three ways a server pushes data to a browser by implementing their wire formats: WebSocket frames, Server-Sent Events and long polling.
chapters.short: WebSocket frames, SSE parser, long-poll broker

chapters.title: Databases in Practice
chapters.goal: Make a slow database fast with your own hands: add the right index, read query plans, kill an N+1, page with keyset pagination, pool connections, and route reads to replicas.
chapters.short: Indexes, query plans, N+1, keyset paging, pooling

chapters.title: Replication, Sharding & Leader Election
chapters.goal: Understand how data is copied and split across machines and how a cluster agrees on a leader: hash vs range partitioning, read-your-writes over async replicas, and Raft-style elections.
chapters.short: Raft votes, partitioners, read-your-writes

chapters.title: Caching Deep Dive: CDN, Edge & Invalidation
chapters.goal: Go beyond cache-aside: build an O(1) LRU, an edge cache with TTL, stale-while-revalidate and tag purges, and versioned asset URLs.
chapters.short: O(1) LRU, edge cache with SWR + tag purge

chapters.title: Async Processing: Queues, Pub/Sub, Events & Cron
chapters.goal: Move slow work off the request path: a work queue with visibility timeouts and a dead-letter queue, a pub/sub event bus, and a cron scheduler you write yourself.
chapters.short: Cron parser, SQS-style queue + DLQ, event bus

chapters.title: Distributed Transactions: 2PC, Sagas, Outbox & Idempotency
chapters.goal: Keep data consistent across services without a single database transaction: two-phase commit, orchestrated sagas with compensations, the transactional outbox and idempotency keys.
chapters.short: 2PC, saga, outbox, idempotency store

chapters.title: Concurrency & Locking
chapters.goal: See race conditions and deadlocks happen, then prevent them: thread-safe code, lock ordering, deadlock detection, optimistic vs pessimistic locking, and distributed locks with leases and fencing tokens.
chapters.short: Lock ordering, deadlock detection, fencing tokens

chapters.title: Memory Leaks & Garbage Collection
chapters.goal: Understand how runtimes free memory and how services still leak it: reference counting vs mark-and-sweep, generational GC, and finding a leak from heap snapshots.
chapters.short: Refcount vs mark-sweep, leak detection

chapters.title: Resilience Patterns
chapters.goal: Make services survive slow and failing dependencies: timeouts and deadlines, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, circuit breakers and backpressure.
chapters.short: Circuit breaker, jittered retries, deadlines, backpressure

chapters.title: Scaling, Serverless & Cost
chapters.goal: Decide how and when to scale and what it costs: target-tracking autoscaling, horizontal vs vertical, serverless cold starts and limits, and break-even maths between serverless and servers.
chapters.short: Target-tracking autoscaler, cold starts, cost maths

chapters.title: Containers & Orchestration
chapters.goal: Learn what Docker and Kubernetes actually do by writing the core loops yourself: a reconciler that drives actual state to desired state, liveness/readiness probes with CrashLoopBackOff, and a service registry with TTL heartbeats.
chapters.short: Reconciler, probes, CrashLoopBackOff, registry

chapters.title: Infrastructure as Code: Terraform & Helm
chapters.goal: Understand the engine behind `terraform plan` and `helm template` by building them small: diff desired vs current state into a plan, order changes by dependency, and render templated manifests from values.
chapters.short: Terraform-style plan + Helm-style templates

chapters.title: CI/CD, Build Caching & Dependencies
chapters.goal: Build the pieces behind every pipeline: semantic version parsing and ranges, a dependency resolver that shows why dependency hell happens, and content-addressed build caching that skips unchanged steps.
chapters.short: Semver ranges, dependency resolver, build cache keys

chapters.title: Deployments & Releases
chapters.goal: Ship changes safely: feature flags with stable percentage rollouts, rolling deployments with surge and unavailability budgets, blue-green switches, canary analysis and fast rollbacks.
chapters.short: Flags, rolling plans, canary analysis, blue-green

chapters.title: Observability: Logs, Metrics, Traces & SLOs
chapters.goal: Know what your system is doing and whether users are happy: structured logs, metrics, distributed tracing with W3C trace context, SLIs and SLOs, error budgets and burn-rate alerts.
chapters.short: Traceparent, JSON logs, error budgets, burn rate

chapters.title: Identity, Secrets & Encryption
chapters.goal: Build the security plumbing every service needs: JWTs with key rotation, OAuth's PKCE, IAM policy evaluation, secret redaction, and envelope encryption at rest and TLS in transit.
chapters.short: JWT kid rotation, PKCE, IAM, redaction

chapters.title: Web Application Security
chapters.goal: Attack and defend a small web app: CORS, CSRF, SQL injection, XSS, SSRF, plus the edge defences (WAF rules and DDoS protection).
chapters.short: CORS, CSRF, XSS, SQLi, SSRF, WAF

chapters.title: Schema Evolution: Migrations & Versioning
chapters.goal: Change databases and data formats without downtime: a versioned migration runner with checksums and rollback, the expand/contract pattern, and upcasters for versioned records and events.
chapters.short: Migration runner with checksums, upcasters

chapters.title: Reliability & Disaster Recovery
chapters.goal: Plan for the bad day: backups with retention and restore drills, failure detection and failover to the most up-to-date replica, multi-region routing, and chaos experiments that prove it works.
chapters.short: GFS backups, failover by LSN, geo routing, chaos

chapters.title: Production Incidents, On-Call & Postmortems
chapters.goal: Practise the human side of operating systems: classify and run incidents, measure detection and recovery times, build a fair on-call rotation and write blameless postmortems.
chapters.short: Severity, MTTx, rotations, blameless postmortems
